# A #[foreign] mark reaches codegen. The struct and its fields are named the
# way the mark says — the same path a js: import's declarations take — and
# nothing was imported to say so: example.com/api does not exist.

sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html --out=out app.sngl
exists out/index.html

# The struct literal and the field read are spelled the module's way.
grep 'Title:' out/index.html
grep '\.Title' out/index.html

# ... and not SNGL's.
! grep 'title:' out/index.html

# The mark names the language it speaks for. The same mark under a go: path
# leaves JavaScript alone — a field name from another language would be a name
# nothing in the generated program answers to.
sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html --out=outgo goapp.sngl
grep 'title:' outgo/index.html
! grep 'Title:' outgo/index.html

# And the path really is unresolvable, which is what makes the build above
# evidence rather than a coincidence: the mark resolved nothing.
! sngl check needsimport.sngl
stderr 'example.com/api'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:std"

#[foreign("js:example.com/api", "Entry")]
struct Entry {
    #[foreign("Title")]
    title string
}

component main {
    var e = Entry{title = "hello"}
    text(value=e.title)
}

-- goapp.sngl --
import . "sngl:std"

#[foreign("go:example.com/api", "api.Entry")]
struct Entry {
    #[foreign("Title")]
    title string
}

component main {
    var e = Entry{title = "hello"}
    text(value=e.title)
}

-- needsimport.sngl --
import . "sngl:std"
import api "js:example.com/api"

component main {
    text(value=string(api.anything()))
}
